source_text: ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ, φέρων τε τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως, ⸂δι’ αὑτοῦ⸃ καθαρισμὸν ⸂τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ποιησάμενος⸃ ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τῆς μεγαλωσύνης ἐν ὑψηλοῖς,
english_snapshot: He[a], being the radiance of his glory and the exact imprint of his being, and sustaining all things by the word of his power, after making purification for sins through himself[b], sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high[c],

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit "through himself"; the phrase is included here following the SBLGNT reading. Traditional English versions often reflect a different textual form, sometimes rendered "by himself."

source_text: τὸν δὲ βραχύ τι παρ’ ἀγγέλους ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον, ὅπως ⸀χωρὶς θεοῦ ὑπὲρ παντὸς γεύσηται θανάτου.
english_snapshot: But we see Jesus[a], who was made lower than the angels for a little while, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'apart from God' instead of 'by the grace of God.'

source_text: πιστὸν ὄντα τῷ ποιήσαντι αὐτὸν ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ⸀ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: who was faithful to the one who appointed him[b][a], just as Moses also was in all his house.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'in all his house,' closely echoing Numbers 12:7; others read simply 'in his house.' The phrase likely refers to God's house.

source_text: καὶ γάρ ἐσμεν εὐηγγελισμένοι καθάπερ κἀκεῖνοι, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ὠφέλησεν ὁ λόγος τῆς ἀκοῆς ἐκείνους, μὴ ⸀συγκεκερασμένους τῇ πίστει τοῖς ἀκούσασιν.
english_snapshot: For indeed[a], we also have had good news proclaimed to us, just as they did; but the message they heard did not benefit them[b], because it was not united by faith with those who heard.

signals.text: Or, following a textual variant and traditional rendering: 'because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard.'

source_text: Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν ⸀γενομένων ἀγαθῶν διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελειοτέρας σκηνῆς οὐ χειροποιήτου, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως,
english_snapshot: But the Messiah came as high priest of the good things that have come[a], through the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made by hands—that is[b], not of this creation—

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'of the good things to come.'

source_text: καὶ γὰρ τοῖς ⸀δεσμίοις συνεπαθήσατε, καὶ τὴν ἁρπαγὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς προσεδέξασθε, γινώσκοντες ἔχειν ⸀ἑαυτοὺς κρείττονα ⸀ὕπαρξιν καὶ μένουσαν.
english_snapshot: For you also suffered together with the prisoners[a], and you accepted with joy the plundering of your possessions[b], knowing that you yourselves have a better and lasting possession.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'knowing that you have for yourselves a better possession in heaven, and one that lasts.'

source_text: ὁ δὲ δίκαιός ⸀μου ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται, καὶ ἐὰν ὑποστείληται, οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ.
english_snapshot: But my righteous one will live by faith[a], and if he shrinks back[c][b], my soul takes no pleasure in him.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read simply 'the righteous one' instead of 'my righteous one.'

source_text: πίστει Ἰακὼβ ἀποθνῄσκων ἕκαστον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰωσὴφ εὐλόγησεν, καὶ προσεκύνησεν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον τῆς ῥάβδου αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: By faith Jacob[a], as he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph[b], and worshiped while leaning on the top of his staff.

signals.text: Or, following the Hebrew text of Genesis 47:31, 'and bowed in worship over the head of his bed.' The Greek text here reads 'staff.'

source_text: Ἀναλογίσασθε γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν εἰς ⸀ἑαυτοὺς ἀντιλογίαν, ἵνα μὴ κάμητε ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν ἐκλυόμενοι.
english_snapshot: For consider the one who endured such opposition from sinners against himself[a], so that you may not grow weary[b], becoming discouraged in your souls.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'against himself'; the SBLGNT text reads 'against themselves.' The sense in context is opposition directed against Jesus.

source_text: οὐκ ἔφερον γὰρ τὸ διαστελλόμενον· Κἂν θηρίον θίγῃ τοῦ ὄρους, λιθοβοληθήσεται·
english_snapshot: For they could not endure what was being commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain[a], it will be stoned.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts add, “or shot with an arrow,” echoing Exodus 19:12–13.
